newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-rail boss to face new enrichment probe.
newsitem.headline: French ex-rail boss to face new enrichment probe.

text.p: France's former railways chairman Loik Le Floch-Prigent, currently detained in a corruption inquiry, faces a new investigation into suspicion of personal enrichment with corporate funds, justice sources said on Friday.

Le Floch-Prigent resigned in July after being held in custody on suspicion of abuse of corporate funds, receiving proceeds of fraud and issuing false information and accounts when he headed French oil giant Elf Aquitaine.

The sources said the Paris public prosecutor had given investigating magistrate Eva Joly instructions to widen her corruption probe to Le Floch-Prigent's purchase of a holiday villa in the Orne region, work on the house, and expenses paid out of an Elf Aquitaine account.
The sources said a total of some nine million francs ($1.8 million) had been invested in the villa.

Lawyers for Le Floch-Prigent, whose application for release from custody have been rejected three times, said they planned to demand all or part of the investigations be declared null and void on legal grounds.
